text:
clair: Starting a lightweight entitlement sweep now (11:00 PT). Scope: admin principals with no console/API activity in 30--90d window, KMS grants to cross-project/service principals, and service accounts referenced only in cron metadata. Aim: evidence tickets + a prioritized dry-run report. No automated removals.
benji: Couple asks: 1) surface grants to external (non-@redwood) domains as top risk, 2) mark any keys used by terraform as infra-owned so infra gets first pass.
aman: We'll diff terraform state vs ownership registry and add tag infra_state=true for tracked bindings. Untracked ones get ownership_missing.
sec-bot: recert-light run rl-20260428-01 started at 2026-04-28T18:00:12Z. Collecting bindings, KMS grants, cron references and last-auth events. Progress updates will be posted.
sre-solo: Owner notifications historically hit oncall. Please add header X-Notify-Quiet and throttle to 30/hr. Also include an explicit "suppress-if-oncall" flag for aliases in the owner registry.
irma: For prioritization, can we rely on enriched log coverage? If audit logs are partial for older projects we should surface "log_gap=true" so reviewers know to request manual proof.
clair: Yes  pipeline will annotate log_gap where retention < 90d. We'll also include last-3-actors for trace.
aman: Splunk query I'm putting in the runbook to find stale decrypts (adapt to your cluster):
```
index=cloud_audit sourcetype=google:kms protoPayload.methodName="Decrypt"
| stats latest(_time) as last_ts, values(protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail) as actors by resource.labels.key_name
| where last_ts < relative_time(now(), "-30d@d")
| sort last_ts asc
```
This gives key, last_ts, and actor list; tag external domains via lookup.
benji: Nice. I'll take ownership of high-risk external keys (top 15) and ping partner teams before owner tickets go out.
sec-bot: collection finished at 2026-04-28T18:03:28Z 1,980 bindings scanned, 104 KMS grants, 37 cron-only SAs, 49 principals with no activity 30--90d, 28 infra_state=false (untracked). Creating 112 owner-evidence tickets and a dry-run revoke report.
irma: For dry-run, please produce two views: 1) conservative (exclude cron-only + infra_state=true + rotation_recent) and 2) aggressive (include infra-untracked but still require manual signoff). Post both CSVs.
clair: Good call. We'll produce both; conservative will be default for owner emails. 5-day owner response window before escalation. If external principal + decrypt activity + ownerless, escalate immediately to ir-team for incident review.
aman: Adding runbook link: /runbooks/entitlement/recert-light.md. It contains steps for verifying ownership, request templates, and emergency rollback.
benji: Template suggestion: include last-use snippet, terraform-tracked flag, log_gap flag, and two quick actions "Confirm ownership" or "Request help" (both open a ticket). Keep the email subject prefix: [Access Light Recert].
sre-solo: I'll add a small oncall suppression script so owner aliases in the registry can be auto-snoozed for 2 hours during the initial blast to reduce pages.
sec-bot: dry-run reports created: recert-light-3598765432-conservative.csv and recert-light-3598765432-aggressive.csv. Tickets created: recert-light-3598765432-112. Tags: ownership_missing(28), external-principal(31), cron_only(37), infra_state_tracked(76), log_gap(12).
clair: Thanks team. After owner responses we will post the conservative dry-run again showing what would be revoked (no changes). Manual revokes only by oncall with checklist. :white_check_mark:
